body:
TO ADVISOR AND PRODUCT.

PR #2034 (BUG-1460) — CHANGES REQUESTED at dd5f259819, narrowly, and it is much closer than the
last two. Leading with what improved, because it is evidence a fix propagated between PRs.

THE AUTHOR DEFENDED AGAINST THE PR-2033 DEFECT. The structural test uses
concat!("wait_for_checks_to_", "register(") and concat!("impl auto_complete::PhaseDriver ",
"for RealPhaseDriver {") — deliberately splitting the literals so the searched strings do not
appear contiguously in the test's own source. That is exactly the bug I found an hour ago, where
include_str! plus split_once matched the test's own literals and scanned 93 characters of
itself. This test CAN fail: remove wait_for_checks_to_register and the first assertion goes red.
Your revert-and-show-it-red rule should still be applied before merge, but the trap was
anticipated.

And criterion 4 is properly met — ci_terminal_sha / ci_terminal_green are written into the
verdict artifact and a real behavioural test reads the JSON back and asserts both. A verdict
recording the CI conclusion it saw, tested the way the rest should be.

BLOCKING ON CRITERION 5 ONLY. "Regression test reproduces the observed ordering: reviewer phase
entered before the reviewed commit's checks have started." The test does not reproduce that. It
asserts that the byte offset of `let current = pr_head_sha_best_effort` is less than the offset
of `mark_drain_phase(Phase::Reviewer)` in the source. Source order is not execution order —
either line could move into a branch, a closure or behind an early return and the assertion
would still pass.

The remedy is in-tree and I named it: MockPhaseDriver in auto_complete.rs already drives
orchestrate() through phases, and BUG-1447 used it exactly this way today in
orchestrate_branch_policy_refusal_never_rebases_or_retries. A driver whose CI phase reports
PrNoChecks and whose head advances mid-phase reproduces the real thing. This is a merge-safety
bug whose own evidence includes two APPROVALS issued while builds were still running, so the
guard is worth a behavioural test rather than a positional one.

A QUESTION I CHECKED AND WILL NOT ASSERT, and the checking is the point. The no_ci_wait
short-circuit inside finish_ci is removed, so a CI phase that runs now always waits. I grepped
lib.rs, got ZERO remaining uses, and was about to report that the documented
`lifecycle:no-ci-wait` tag had been silently made a no-op against CLAUDE.md line 160. A
full-workspace search shows 14 live uses in auto_complete.rs, including the orchestrator branch
at 3794 that can skip the CI phase outright. The tag is not dead and my draft claim was false.

That is the second time today a single-file search would have produced a wrong finding, and the
first time I caught it myself rather than being corrected. The habit that caught it is the one
from this morning's memory: the search that produced an interesting answer is the one to re-run
unbounded.

What I could not settle by grepping: whether any spec that relied on the finish_ci escape now
waits where CLAUDE.md promises it will not. I asked the author to confirm, and to update
CLAUDE.md in the same change if a documented tag's behaviour moved.

ONE NON-BLOCKING FIXTURE BUG, one character. The new fake-gh line is
`if [ "$1 $2" = "pr view" ]` under set -eu, while the line directly above correctly guards
`${1:-}`. Demonstrated: one argument gives "parameter not set" exit 2, zero arguments likewise.
Use `"${1:-} ${2:-}"`. I also confirmed the module is cfg(all(test, unix)) — so this is NOT an
instance of BUG-1475's Windows fake-binary class, and I recorded that so nobody fixes it in the
wrong direction.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
